title: Wayfare Pass Correction-Timing Relief on Ride Credit — Desk Guidance
content:
# Correction-timing relief — Wayfare Pass (rider membership)

## Rule the desk applies

When Pass ride credit is clawed back from a Wayfare Pass member because a fare was reduced by a fare adjustment, the correction-timing relief follows the calendar days from the fare charge date to the fare adjustment date: 25 percent at 7 days or more, 10 percent at 3 to 6 days, nothing under 3 days.

The relief takes that percentage of the clawed-back credit on the trip off the credit correction. The percentage is of the clawed-back credit itself; the credit correction never goes below 0.00, and it is rounded half up to the cent once the relief is taken off.

## Dates read

Both dates come from the trip's charges in Wayfare Rides (rider trips and fares): the date of the fare charge and the date of the fare adjustment booked against it.

| Calendar days from fare charge date to fare adjustment date | Relief |
|---|---|
| 7 or more | 25 percent |
| 3 to 6 | 10 percent |
| 0 to 2 | nothing |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical dates)

- Fare charged 1 May, adjusted 8 May: 7 days, 25 percent. Adjusted 7 May: 6 days, 10 percent.
- Fare charged 1 May, adjusted 4 May: 3 days, 10 percent. Adjusted 3 May: 2 days, nothing.

## Figure (hypothetical)

With 1.80 clawed back and an adjustment 9 days after the fare charge, 0.45 is taken off, leaving 1.35.
